title: S3e promotion framework, hermes-eval suite and success metrics: features cache_aware_context, steering_policy, stale_steering, fast_path, memory_tiers with self-refusing criteria; deterministic P34 evals; scorecard --hermes (P33, P34, P35)
spec:
orchestrator/promotion.py: ensure FEATURES holds cache_aware_context (context_router cache_mode plus tool and skill cache_mode as one feature with three config keys), steering_policy, stale_steering, fast_path and memory_tiers, each with criteria expressed like the existing entries: minimum shadow sample size (30 rows, or 20 for steering kinds), non-inferior quality (first-pass rate and fix-round rate of affected tasks not worse than the shadow baseline), improved accepted-goal economics (effective tokens or usd per accepted goal lower), plus a fresh passing hermes-eval within 7 days; demotion when a regression of the same metrics persists over 10 tasks. Create orchestrator/hermes_eval.py with deterministic cases over temp fixtures: memory (delegate to memory_eval), cache (stable prefix identical across two tasks of one role and goal; dynamic suffix differs; telemetry normalize and effective cost correct; stable tool catalog unchanged between two tasks), worker control (inspect lists a fake running worker; steer records before delivery; cancel releases pool capacity and retains the partial; replacement packet carries prior_worker facts), security (a malicious external skill fixture is high risk and cannot move to testing; a malicious agents file scans blocked; fake authority escalation blocked; a secret exfiltration instruction blocked; a harmless security document is not blocked), fast path (a trivial fixture task is level 0 or 1 with the skip list; a security-path task never below 4; an architectural task 4; a fast-path task with two fix rounds triggers the demotion rule). run(root) persists .orchestrator/hermes_eval.json; CLI `orchestrator hermes-eval [--json]`. orchestrator/scorecard.py: `orchestrator scorecard --hermes` prints the P35 metrics in one table from the existing scorecards and the new modules: accepted-goal success, first-pass, fix-round rate, tokens and effective uncached tokens and usd and latency per accepted goal; HOT memory tokens, retrieval precision and usefulness, compaction count; cache hit ratio, cache-read, uncached, invalidations, effective context cost; steering rate and success, cancellations, partial-result reuse, fix rounds avoided; suspicious context detected, false-positive rate (suspicious later marked safe by a human transition reason), blocked imports; orchestration amplification, cost share, latency share. Docs: docs/hermes-hardening/19-promotion-and-evals.md.
Spec review T-1319 folded in: (1) No multi-key entry: register three single-key features context_cache ([context_router].cache_mode), tool_cache ([tool_disclosure].cache_mode) and skill_cache ([skills].cache_mode); the docs group them as cache-aware disclosure. (2) Refusal lives in promotion.evaluate: it returns stay with reason hermes_eval_missing_or_stale when .orchestrator/hermes_eval.json is missing, malformed, future-dated, older than 7 days or not passed; the self-refusal callers that already consult evaluate before running active (skill routing, fast_path, steering_policy) therefore refuse; evaluate never changes config. (3) stale_steering = the stale-severity trigger of steering policy shipped by T-1316: table [steering], key stale_mode (T-1316 adds it, default shadow), evidence = steering rows with trigger stale_severity; this task depends on T-1316. (4) The new criteria are ADDITIVE and apply only to the five new features (context_cache, tool_cache, skill_cache, steering_policy's stale trigger, memory_tiers); existing bespoke branches (fast_path min 20 and its two-fix-round demote, steering_policy min 20) are unchanged and their tests stay green. (5) Demotion is stateless: computed on every call from the last 10 task rows of the feature; economics 'improved' with a None metric means stay (missing data never promotes); shadow and active cohorts are disjoint sets of task ids. (6) hermes_eval.json records ran_at (ISO, Europe/Zurich), cases [{name, passed, detail}] and passed; run(root, now=None) and the freshness check take an injectable now and read the file from the explicit root argument, never STATE. (7) Every eval case runs against an explicit temp root and public APIs: memory_eval.run(root), cache_telemetry.normalize/effective_cost and tool_catalog.cache_view, worker_control.cancel/steer with the injectable process seams (sleep, alive, signal_fn) and a fake pool, context_scanner.scan, skill_discovery.inspect plus skills_registry.transition, harness_depth.level, evidence.make; no case touches STATE or the real bus.
Spec review T-1324 folded in (overrides earlier wording where they differ): (1) evaluate(feature, evidence, cfg, *, root=None, now=None): the hermes-eval gate applies ONLY to the four new features context_cache, tool_cache, skill_cache and stale_steering (memory_tiers, fast_path and steering_policy keep their existing evaluation unchanged); root None means the gate is skipped with reason eval_root_missing, so existing evaluate tests stay green. (2) Real refusal points: fast_path (harness_depth) and steering_policy (daemon) already consult evaluate; for the three cache features the single reader context_router.cache_mode(cfg, section) (scope adds orchestrator/context_router.py and tests/test_context_router.py) consults promotion.evaluate(feature, collect(...), cfg, root=..., now=...) when the configured value is active and returns shadow with a notify when the verdict is stay; drop the skill-routing claim. (3) memory_tiers keeps its FEATURES entry and generic path unchanged; it gains only the stateless demotion computed from its own rows. (4) stale_steering FEATURES entry: table steering, key stale_mode (T-1316 is merged on this branch and adds the key; a missing or invalid value yields default shadow with invalid_config on the collect result, never active), evidence = decision_log rows of kind steering with trigger stale_severity counted per mode. (5) Cohorts: a task belongs to the shadow or active cohort by the mode of its rows for that feature (a task with both is counted once, as active); first-pass rate = tasks without a fix round (no task with constraints.fix_round_for equal to it) over the cohort, fix-round rate = mean fix rounds per task, both from the bus under the given root; fewer than 10 active tasks -> stay (no demotion decision); demotion when the mean over the last 10 active tasks is worse than the shadow mean on either rate; collect() gains branches for context_cache, tool_cache, skill_cache and stale_steering; tests use a synthetic decision_log and tasks fixture under a temp root.
Repository rules: unittest (not pytest), tests/_harness.py single ORCH_ROOT fixture; every acceptance test id tests/test_<module>.py::test_name is a method def test_name(self) in a unittest.TestCase. No new third-party dependencies. Never write secret values to any file or log; test fixtures use synthetic names and values that are not credential-shaped. Do not quote template placeholder tokens (double braces) anywhere in code comments or docs. Shadow-first: a new adaptive path never changes what a worker sees until its mode is active; shadow only writes decision_log or runs rows. Task worktrees carry no .orchestrator runs, tasks or decision_log state: tests use synthetic fixtures; for any measured numbers in docs run read-only against /Users/k3ntaw/code/orchestrator/.orchestrator via an explicit root argument. Run .claude/hooks/tests-green.sh . until green; the base suite must stay green. Do not ask questions: decide, and note decisions in the result summary. Contracts of the earlier modules: .orchestrator/plan.md (section GOAL T-0991) and docs/hermes-hardening/*.md on this branch; read the merged modules before building on them.
